headline: High risk of prompt injection and data leakage: Cursor’s shared filesystem, clipboard, and broad egress can expose or act on content while the paired sample repo offers no isolation or verification controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor ingests workspace files, open buffers, clipboard, and MCP content by default, and can auto-run tools in Yolo mode. The spring-integration-samples repo is a codebase with no documented provenance or isolation controls, so malicious content in shared files could steer Cursor’s agent loop. The interaction is plausible, but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF the two agents share a local workspace or clipboard bridge, injected instructions in files can reach Cursor's agent loop.
IF Cursor is run in Yolo mode, tool calls may execute without approval.
mitigations: Disable Yolo mode for the session.
Separate the agents into different workspaces.
Clear clipboard before copying between agents.
Require manual review of any file content before Cursor acts on it.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for shared files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, and clipboard contents, and has broad network egress to model providers and MCP servers. The sample repo is open-source and may be used as shared workspace content, so sensitive local files could flow from Cursor into remote inference. The repo itself does not add protections, so the leakage path remains plausible.
conditions: IF sensitive files are opened in the shared workspace, Cursor can read them and send them to external model providers.
IF the same local filesystem is used for both agents, file contents can be exposed across the pair.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared workspace.
Use a separate OS user or profile for Cursor.
Disable or restrict network egress for the session.
Avoid pasting secrets into the clipboard.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor can write the filesystem, modify git state, execute shell commands, and spawn subprocesses; the paired repo is a mutable codebase. With shared local filesystem state and no locking documented for the repo, concurrent edits or git operations can collide and overwrite work. Because defaults allow broad mutation, the conflict risk is high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same checkout, concurrent writes can race.
IF either agent commits or rewrites git state without coordination, one agent can overwrite the other's changes.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Use git locks or a single-writer policy.
Review diffs before committing.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor’s agent loop can generate code or actions from its own outputs, while the sample repo provides no verification layer or downstream checks. If one agent’s output is copied into the other’s workflow, errors can cascade into incorrect edits or commands. The pathway exists, but the blast radius is limited to work products rather than immediate irreversible harm.
conditions: IF outputs from one agent are treated as authoritative input by the other, mistakes can propagate.
IF the repo is used as a source of instructions or examples, incorrect assumptions can be repeated.
mitigations: Require human verification of cross-agent outputs.
Add a checklist before executing generated commands.
Compare outputs against the repo’s actual files.
Limit one agent to drafting only.
requires-engineering: add automated validation gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor is a closed-source editor that can send content to external model providers, while the sample repo is open-source and does not itself indicate regulated data handling. No specific residency or certification mismatch is documented for the pair, so only a low compliance concern is justified from the documented remote-processing behavior.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Cursor, it may be transmitted to external providers.
IF the repo is repurposed to store regulated data, the lack of documented controls becomes relevant.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in the workspace.
Review vendor privacy settings.
Use redacted sample data only.
Keep compliance-sensitive work in a separate environment.
requires-engineering: obtain formal DPA and residency review.
